conditional_scope: Formula/specification review only; no empirical assumption, originality, GPU interface or efficacy verified.

formal_object.rationale: A full coordinate trajectory y; anchored free coordinates z; second time-difference D2 with actual timestep units; positive observation metric M. The stated object/domain, rather than the official unsquared Chamfer, is the object of this conditional derivation.

operations_and_conditions.rationale: A01: Second differences at physical/native timesteps -> Acceleration-scaled temporal operator; condition: Timestamps and time units are retained; C02: Group norm lambda sum ||(D2 y)_t,v||_2 -> Dual balls preserve sparse dynamic events; condition: Convex group-norm domain; D04: Quadratic data fit plus acceleration sparsity -> Convex group-trend repair; condition: Positive definite observation metric and exact anchor constraints All current edges remain conditional where model/data availability is not established.

derivation.rationale: The vector group norm has a Euclidean dual ball, changing the prior from uniform quadratic acceleration. On y=y_p+Sz, stationarity keeps S^T M(y_p+Sz-yhat), including anchor and off-diagonal metric contributions. Physical timestep scaling is explicit. No event recovery or real-motion preservation is proved.

assumptions.rationale: Conditional validity requires: Real motion need not be piecewise velocity; sinusoidal or rapidly articulated motion can be biased.; Groups are 3D vectors, avoiding an arbitrary axis-wise L1 convention.; Tuning and timestamp scaling are frozen before confirmation.; Acceleration sparsity is an inference prior, not a new benchmark metric or event label. These are obligations, not observations about ActionBench.

method_expression.rationale: Apply anchored group trend filtering to native coordinates with the same original timestamps; preserve all motion events the optimizer retains. The reviewed construction is Nonsmooth group acceleration sparsity rather than quadratic smoothing or low-rank estimation.. This is a specification, not an implemented method.

prediction_and_falsifier.rationale: The construction predicts: Sparse abrupt changes should survive better than equal-strength Gaussian smoothing; smooth high-frequency real motion can be a failure boundary. It can be rejected by: Reject if Gaussian/second-order quadratic smoothing at equal tuning/compute matches official CD-M and geometry, or if event-like true motion is suppressed. This contrast is specified before any new-method experiment.

closest_alternative.rationale: Named alternatives: Classical trend filtering and STAC Gaussian temporal smoothing. Claimed operational difference: Changes the temporal regularity prior and dual constraint, not the Gaussian bandwidth; existing trend filtering is attributed. This check verifies an explicit comparator and conditional delta, not completed novelty clearance.
